description: Algeria's National Statistics Office published in 2011 the urban framework report of the 2008 General Population and Housing Census (RGPH 2008), built from the exhaustive census results. It lists the country's 851 urban agglomerations with their population and urban stratum, from metropolitan to semi-urban, and shows that 137 of them form 37 intercommunal urban agglomerations, while 237 became urban between 1998 and 2008. Further tables give population and density by wilaya and planning region, rural and semi-rural agglomerations, and a classification of all communes as urban or rural. The Algerian definition of an urban agglomeration makes connection to the drinking water, electricity and sanitation networks a mandatory condition, next to size, non-agricultural employment and facilities such as hospitals and schools. Coverage is national. Format and access: a free 214 page PDF in the ONS Collections Statistiques series (n° 163); the ONS site also serves RGPH 2008 national population tables. Licence: not stated on the pages read. Caveats: tables are inside a PDF, not a machine readable file; results of the 2022 census (RGPH 2022) are not yet on the ONS site beyond posters, and the RGPH 2020 page returned a server error. Simulation uses: settlement hierarchy and urban growth as a base for network expansion planning and population exposure by agglomeration. Related records: the ARPCE Algeria market observatories.
